sources.entry: Lura - High-performance API Gateway. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Go

summary.one_liner: Lura is an open Go framework (formerly the KrakenD framework) for assembling high-performance API gateways and proxies out of middleware and reusable components.
summary.what_it_does: Lura is a set of generic Go libraries for building API gateways and proxies that sit between clients and backend servers. It can aggregate responses from several backend sources into a single endpoint, and lets you group, wrap, transform and shrink those responses so clients receive only the fields they need. The README states it supports HTTP(S) and, because it is a generic library set, can be used to build other gateway types such as an RPC gateway. It is designed to be extended with your own middleware through small, independent components. The README's example shows a Go program that parses a JSON configuration file, sets up a logger, and runs a Gin-based router with the proxy factory. The repository is the source code; the README points to the KrakenD binary for a ready-to-run gateway.
use_cases: build a custom API gateway in Go
aggregate multiple backend APIs into one endpoint
trim and reshape JSON responses for mobile or UI clients
reuse proxy components in another Go application
build a non-HTTP RPC gateway from generic libraries
how_to_run: Add the library to your Go module: import github.com/luraproject/lura/v3 packages (config, logging, proxy, router/gin)
Write a main.go that parses a configuration file with config.NewParser()
Compile and run the program with your configuration file
notable: Generic library set: can be used to build HTTP gateways or other kinds of proxies such as RPC gateways
Aggregates several backend sources into single endpoints and reshapes responses
Formerly known as the KrakenD framework and is the core service of the KrakenD API Gateway
Designed for custom middleware and small, reusable, Unix-style components
caveats: It is a library, not a ready-to-use gateway; you need Go and must write your own application (the README points to the KrakenD binary for a turnkey gateway)
The README's configuration file section is a placeholder with no details, so configuration must be learned from the external documentation
keywords: combine multiple api calls into one
